sara wang: Heads-up — after the http2 small-write optimization landed in canary we see a host-ingest perf regression. KV cache miss rate jumped ~3x and p95 tail doubled. Attaching short flame and a few traces below.

sara wang: flame (short): ingress_parse -> tokenization -> kv_cache_lookup shows a lot more short-lived shards and evictions. writev count also increased (~2.8x).

sara wang: trace snippet:
```
[ingest] writev_calls=1834 -> 5123
[kv] evictions/sec=12 -> 38
[latency] p95_ms=42 -> 89
syscalls: send(2)->send(7) spike on per-request path
```

david k: which PR? any obvious change to the proxy coalesce logic?

sara wang: PR 1452 — it switched to immediate flush for frames under threshold to lower latency on tiny responses. probably causing more fragmented buffers that hit the parser slow path.

jun park: iirc fragmented frames cause extra allocations in host preproc because we re-enter parse state machine more often. that increases short-lived objects and thrashes the kv cache hot-shard.

rachel t: simplest quick mitigation: re-enable coalescing in the ingress proxy while we debug. set write_coalesce_ms back to 5ms or increase write buffer to 8KB. that'll reduce small writes and hopefully lower kv eviction pressure.

leo m: also check batching heuristics — if upstream now sends more tiny frames we might be autoclosing batches early. the autobatcher uses "min_batch_bytes" and a per-conn timeout. small writes can make it commit tiny batches and hit kernel selection for small-seq paths (worse exec kernels).

sara wang: added two small logs to canary to print batch size and kernel selection path. sample: `batch_bytes=340 kernel=small-seq-kern`

ops-bot: deploy canary/ingress-proxy@canary-1452 started by sara wang at 6272469200

david k: can we reproduce locally with a replay? i can run a 5k req replay with the new ingress behavior and capture kvcache metrics. also add metric: ingress.writev_count and host.kv_evictions to dashboards.

jun park: note that kvcache eviction here looks like hot-shard contention rather than total capacity. small fragmented requests interleave keys causing poor locality. adding a per-conn prefix-caching hint might help until we fix framing.

rachel t: Agree on two-step approach: (1) quick revert/coalesce on canary to stabilize; (2) update batching heuristics to prefer merging tiny writes into existing batches (increase min_batch_bytes from 256 to 1024 and bump batch_hold_ms to 3).

leo m: one more thought — kernel selection currently picks small-seq kernels for <=512 tokens. If fragmented framing forces many sub-requests below that threshold we pay kernel switching overhead. Consider an adaptive heuristic: if avg_batch_bytes < threshold for N sec then bias toward medium-seq kernel to amortize switching cost.

sara wang: thanks. i'll roll the coalesce revert to canary now and kick off david's replay. if that looks good i'll promote. patch I'll apply:
```diff
- write_coalesce_ms = 0 // immediate flush
+ write_coalesce_ms = 5 // re-enable coalesce for small frames
- min_batch_bytes = 256
+ min_batch_bytes = 1024
+ batch_hold_ms = 3
```

sara wang: ping me if you see the canary metrics change (p95, kv_evictions, writev_count). i'll post results in ~20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
